summary.oneLiner: Banaras Beads Limited is a Varanasi-based, Government-of-India recognised Export House manufacturing and exporting handicraft glass beads, necklaces and imitation jewellery to reputed customers across the USA, Europe and Japan.
summary.business: The Company manufactures and exports handicraft items such as glass beads, necklaces and imitation jewellery, produced largely by hand and on small machines at Varanasi. Its products are sold to reputed international customers in the U.S.A., U.K., France, Germany, Japan and other countries, and it has also initiated indigenous online and offline sales in India under the name De-Lemon. All of these items form a single reportable segment, with commercial activity concentrated at Varanasi.

Handicrafts (single segment): Articles of gold, silver and other precious and semi-precious metal and stone

currentContext.expansion: The only expansion initiative disclosed in this annual report is a diversification: the Company states it is in the process of expanding its business by developing a Logistic Park / Godown to earn additional income, and that it purchased some land for this purpose during the year. No project cost, site name, size, or commissioning/ramp timeline is given. Beyond that, management describes ongoing development of new items/products on which orders are being received, and continued efforts on quality control, cost reduction and widening the marketing network. There was no change in the nature of the business during the year, and manufacturing remains concentrated at Varanasi, which the Company gives as the reason no separate geographical segment reporting is required. No new plant, capacity addition, debottlenecking, acquisition or joint venture is mentioned.
currentContext.mdna: Management states that demand for the Company's products is increasing day by day in both the international and indigenous markets, supported by new items/products on which orders are being received.|The Company's products are fashionable items made by hand/small machines and take time in production; a change of fashion over a short period directly affects demand for the products in the market.|The products of the Company are appreciated in the international market and are sold to various reputed customers in the U.S.A., U.K., France, Germany, Japan and other countries.|Fluctuation in foreign currency prices affected the profit of the Company, given the export-oriented business model.|The planned Logistic Park / Godown is intended to generate additional income beyond the core handicrafts business.|Management flags that global and supply conditions, input availability and prices, changes in Government regulations, foreign policy, foreign currency, tax laws and domestic economic developments could significantly impact operations.|Qualitative only: "The Company is developing new items/products and getting order on the basis of same" — no order-book value, pipeline size or execution period is disclosed anywhere in the routed sections.

risks.note: "The main business of your Company is Export business" — the Company is a recognised Export House selling to the U.S.A., U.K., France, Germany, Japan and other markets, so revenue and profitability are directly geared to overseas demand and to conditions in a handful of developed markets rather than to the domestic economy.

Management explicitly flags that "the long-term continuation of War between US and Iran may affect business of the company upto some limit in coming periods", i.e. an external conflict is expected to bear on the export franchise.

The Company's products are "fashionable items" and "the change of fashion in sort [short] period directly affects demand of products in market" — demand can turn quickly and inventory/product development can be stranded, which is structural for a handicraft jewellery exporter.

"The fluctuation in foreign currency price also affected the profit of the Company" — stated as having already hit profit this year, not as a hypothetical; with essentially all sales invoiced abroad there is a direct translation/transaction exposure.

Management names "change in duty drawback, DEPB, Exchange Rate, custom duty on Import/Export and Government policies" as having a direct effect on profitability — export incentives are a real component of realisations and are set by policy the Company does not control.

"Change in interest rate on borrowing and risk of liquidity of current assets would have a direct effect on the profitability of the Company" — a working-capital-heavy, receivables-and-inventory business is exposed to both funding cost and the realisability of those current assets.

All products — glass beads, necklaces, imitation jewellery — "form just one Segment", and "the company has its commercial activity mainly at Varanasi, hence separate geographical segment wise reporting is not required". There is no second business or second manufacturing base to absorb a shock to the handicrafts line or to the Varanasi site.

Products "are being made by hand/small machines and take time in production", with output dependent on small Karigars and village cottage-industry vendors whom the Company itself trains. This limits the ability to scale or respond quickly when fashion turns, and ties throughput to skilled-artisan availability; the permanent workforce was 243 as on March 31, 2026 with no recognised employee association.

risks.risk: Macro and input-cost sensitivity flagged in the forward-looking statement
risks.note: The MD&A cautionary paragraph enumerates "global and supply conditions, input availability and prices, changes in Government regulations, foreign policy, foreign currency, tax laws, economic developments within the country" as factors that could make a significant impact on operations.
